Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, saying delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives and complaining that the US is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks.
In an interview with the BBC at his central Kyiv office, Ukraine's president also said it was "strange" that Donald Trump had posted a photo of himself embracing Vladimir Putin as "my friend".
"Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky said, speaking in English.
"He's an aggressor, and a killer…He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," he said, adding it was like saying you were friends with Adolf Hitler during World War Two.
Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States.
Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv.
The latest round of peace talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress: "The more we know, the more problems", is how Zelensky described it.
He said talks were expected to resume in December.

item.title: [ABC News World] Schizophrenic man found guilty of attempted murders of 14, including 10 on train
item.description:
Schizophrenic man found guilty of attempted murders of 14, including 10 on train
A schizophrenic man has been found guilty of the attempted murders of 14 people over three separate incidents over a 24-hour period that culminated with the stabbing of 10 people on a high-speed London-bound trainByPAN PYLAS Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 12:53 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
LONDON -- A schizophrenic man was found guilty Thursday of the attempted murders of 14 people over three separate incidents over a 24-hour period that culminated with the stabbing of 10 people on a high-speed London-bound train.
Anthony Williams, 33, had admitted carrying out the attacks but denied that he intended to kill. His trial at Cambridge Crown Court was told that he was suffering from an acute psychosis at the time as a result of his schizophrenia.
But he was found guilty of all 14 counts of attempted murder by a jury after 16 hours and 52 minutes of deliberations. Most of the verdicts were unanimous.
Williams started his stabbing rampage on the evening of Oct. 31, 2025, when he knifed a boy and attempted to stab two men in the town of Peterborough, around 75 miles north of the capital.
He then traveled to London, where he stabbed a boy on a metro train in the early hours of Nov. 1, before returning to Peterborough and spending much of the day at home.
That evening, he boarded an LNER train service and stabbed nine passengers and a member of the onboard staff during his five-minute attack.
All survived their injuries.
One of those stabbed, Samir Zitouni, a member of the crew, had life-threatening injuries, having received stab wounds including three to the back while he was trying to fend off Williams with a frying pan. He suffered “catastrophic blood loss” and required four blood transfusions.

item.title: [ABC News World] Spain's former central bank head chosen as next European Central Bank president
item.description:
Spain's former central bank head chosen as next European Central Bank president
Eurozone leaders have chosen a new president of the European Central BankByDAVID MCHUGH Associated Press and SAM MCNEIL Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 10:46 AM
Share
BRUSSELS -- European leaders have chosen the former head of Spain’s central bank, Pablo Hernández de Cos, to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank as the key EU institution confronts inflation driven by the war in Iran and worries about high government debt and borrowing costs in Europe.
Leaders from the 21 European member countries that use the euro also filled two other top posts at the ECB, which decides borrowing costs for the 359 million people in the eurozone.
European Council President António Costa said on X that the body agreed on the three appointments at a summit in Brussels.
De Cos’ nomination still must pass review by the European Parliament and the ECB’s governing council, but those steps are formalities.
The appointment puts an experienced central banker with a reputation for backing lower interest rates and monetary stimulus in charge at a time when several European governments are struggling with heavy debt loads and rising borrowing costs. De Cos, 55, served on the ECB rate-setting council from 2018 to 2024 through his post as head of the Spanish central bank.
A review of his speeches by Commerzbank analysts “suggests that de Cos is among the monetary policy doves,” or policymakers who lean toward lower rates to support growth.
De Cos won out over another main contender for the post, former Netherlands central bank head Klaas Knot, who was regarded as a hawk, or someone who favors higher rates to ward off inflation.

item.title: [CBS News World] Germany arrests 2 Iraqis allegedly tied to Iran-linked terror group
item.description:
Berlin — German authorities on Thursday arrested two Iraqi men on suspicion of terrorism. The suspects are alleged to be members of an Iran-linked terrorist organization that is said to have targeted U.S., Israeli and Jewish institutions in Europe.
The men, who were arrested in Cologne and Heidelberg by the Federal Criminal Police Office, are Iraqi nationals Mostafa Al-R. and Ameer J., according to the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office.
The investigation centers on alleged links to Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya, a shadowy group that emerged to claim a series of sabotage, arson and violent attacks targeting Jewish institutions in Europe not long after the start of the U.S. war with Iran. The U.S. government has labeled HAYI a front for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah in Iraq. Britain has designated HAYI as a terrorist organization.
According to investigators, Mostafa Al-R. is alleged to have maintained contact with Mohammad Al-Saadi, who is currently facing criminal charges in the United States. Al-Saadi is considered a central figure within the alleged terrorist network.
As early as late 2025, Al-Saadi, Mostafa Al-R. and other individuals allegedly founded an independent group whose goal was to carry out terrorist attacks in Germany and other European countries, according to prosecutors. Ameer J. is also a member of this group, they said.
The group planned to target synagogues in Cologne and another European city, prosecutors alleged, saying unknown perpetrators traveled to the locations in March 2026 on behalf of the organization. The plans were not implemented for unknown reasons.
HAYI is also linked to attacks on Jewish institutions in the United Kingdom, France, Belgium and the Netherlands, the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution said.
The suspects are accused of membership in a domestic terrorist organization under Section 129a of Germany's Criminal Code. ...

BUNIA, Congo — The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has topped 12,000 confirmed cases, government data showed Thursday, as fighting between rebels and the army disrupts efforts to contain the spread of the disease.
It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and nearly half the 12,021 people confirmed to have the virus have died, according to data from Congo's Ministry of Health. It is also the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.
The outbreak declared in May is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Response teams are battling armed conflict, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation.

Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis are trading increasingly intense strikes on strategic sites, including oil infrastructure and ports, marking a sharp escalation in fighting between the two sides.
A projectile struck an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s southwestern Jazan region on Thursday, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several others, according to the Saudi Ministry of Energy. The strike sparked a fire and temporarily suspended some operations at the facility, the ministry said.
The attack came a day after the Houthis claimed to have struck Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery at Ras Tanura. Satellite imagery taken Wednesday showed a huge plume of black smoke rising from the coastal peninsula following the attack.

item.title: [ABC News World] Rescuers battle tough conditions in flooded Indonesian mine
item.description:
Rescuers battle tough conditions in flooded Indonesian mine
Rescuers are battling high water, darkness and slippery, narrow terrain while searching for miners believed trapped by flooding in an illegal gold mineByNINIEK KARMINI Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 10:43 PM
JAKARTA, Indonesia -- Rescuers battled high water, darkness and slippery, narrow terrain Thursday searching for 10 miners believed trapped by flooding in an illegal gold mine where 16 bodies have been recovered.
The miners were digging for grains of gold late Monday when heavy rain caused the Ciseureuh River to overflow into a mine shaft in the Bogor regency of West Java province. Several people escaped from one section of the excavation before floodwaters filled the shaft, estimated to be about 100 meters (330 feet) deep, in a mountainous area south of the capital, Jakarta.
Authorities said they were not immediately notified because the miners were operating illegally, and local miners and residents initially tried to pump water from the site themselves before the situation became unmanageable.
Police first received reports of trapped miners about 16 hours after the flooding occurred, and nearby state-owned mining company PT Antam forwarded a formal report to the Jakarta Search and Rescue Agency shortly after midnight Wednesday, triggering a full-scale rescue operation.
The search and rescue team used submersible water pumps to suck water from the hole and tried to close off openings where groundwater seeped in.
West Java police spokesperson Hendra Rochmawan said authorities believe at least 10 miners remain trapped as rescuers retrieved 16 bodies by Thursday.

item.description:

Watch: Christy says she still sends WhatsApp messages to her husband who died in the blazeByGrace Tsoi, BBC World Service, Phoebe Kong, BBC Chinese , Reporting fromHong Kong and Yvette TanPublished25 November 2026
It was a sunny Wednesday afternoon on 26 November last year, and Mrs Lau was attending a dance class at an activity centre close to her home.
At around 14:45 she heard the faint sounds of fire engine sirens - but didn't think much of it.
It was only a while later, when she started receiving calls from a friend, that she found out that Wang Fuk Court - the eight-block apartment complex she had called home for the past 40 years - was ablaze. And her husband - a wheelchair user - was trapped inside their home.
"I grabbed my things quickly and ran down without even putting my shoes on properly," Mrs Lau, who wanted to be identified only by her surname, told the BBC.
When she got there, the building had been cordoned off by police.
She called her 74-year-old husband but he told her not to worry - he hadn't heard an alarm so it was probably a small fire, he said.
Mrs Lau could only watch helplessly as the blaze tore through Wang Fuk Court at a peak speed of about 10m (33ft) per second - an "unprecedented" rate, a final report released by an independent committee in relation to the deadly blaze that killed 168 people found.
It was a tragedy that was entirely preventable but happened as a result of a series of human errors, fire safety failures, alleged fraud and suspected corruption, said the report.
"It was ferocious… I saw the fire jump [from one building to another] - then a huge fireball burst. It was truly hell on Earth. How could anyone possibly escape?" said Mrs Lau.
She tried calling her husband again. This time, there was no answer.
